title: The hawk-eyed songbird: retinal morphology, eye shape, and visual fields of an aerial insectivore
journal: journal and volume not confirmed (Dryad data record 10.5061/dryad.n7140)
why: A swallow (tree swallow, Tachycineta, the Hirundinidae relative of the listed Petrochelidon and Stelgidopteryx) with a bifoveate retina, four foveae in a 100 degree arc, a long eye, a large posterior blind area and a narrow binocular field. No swallow of the listed genera has a measurement, so these would be the nearest measured values if the owner accepts a family-level carry exception for visual field and acuity.
get: open-access address: https://datadryad.org/dataset/doi:10.5061/dryad.n7140 (data record; the article itself via library)

authors: Rodrigues T, Matter MM, Chiodini A, Genton B, Brethaut E, Chiodini F, Matter-Sadzinski L, Matter J-M
title: Foveal vision in fast-flying birds hunting on the wing
why: Swifts and swallows (Hirundo rustica, Delichon urbicum) share temporal foveae; only the abstract was read, which gives one number (large ganglion cell soma area of at least 200 um2). The full text may give foveal cone and ganglion densities for a Hirundinidae relative of Petrochelidon and Stelgidopteryx.
